questions.question: Debenture holders of a company are its _________.
questions.solution:
The ‘debenture’ is derived from the Latin word ‘debere’ which means ‘to owe’.

 
• It is a written instrument that acknowledges a loan to the company and is executed under the company’s common seal.
 
• It contains a contract for the principal amount to be repaid after a specified period or at intervals and for payment of interest at a fixed rate which is usually paid either half-yearly or yearly on fixed dates.
 
• A person having the debentures is called debenture holder. They are the persons or firms who purchase the debentures of other company. They are not concerned with the management and regulation of the company.
 
• Debentures are usually secured and carry a charge on the assets of the company, hence, debenture holders are the secured creditors of the company.

questions.question: Currency notes and coins of one rupee and lower denominations are issued by the _________.
questions.solution:
Currency notes and coins of one rupee and lower denominations are issued by the Ministry of Finance.

 
• Under the Coinage Act, 1906, the Government of India has the sole right to mint coins.
 
• According to the Section 24(1) of the RBI Act, 1934, RBI is not entitled to issue banknote of denomination of value of one rupee.
 
• Also, ‘I promise to pay the bearer’ is not written on the one rupee note.
 
• The currency note of one rupee is issued by the Ministry of Finance and signed by the Finance Secretary of India.

questions.question: Which of the following places is not a Middle Stone Age?
questions.solution:
Of the following, Ganeshwar is not the place of Middle Stone Age.

 
• The site of Ganeshwar is located close to the copper mines of Sikar-Jhunjhunu copper belt of Rajasthan.
 
• There were many copper objects excavated from the area that included spearhead, arrowhead, chisel, bangles, and many microliths that were characteristic of the Chalcolithic Culture.
 
• People of Chalcolithic age used objects made of stone and copper.
 
• Ganeshwar predate the mature Harappan Culture.

questions.question: The title of Persian translation of the Mahabharata is: __________.
questions.solution:
The title of the Persian translation of the Mahabharata is __**Razmanama**__.

 
• In Persian, ‘Razm’ means ‘war’, and ‘nama’ means ‘tale’. So, Razmnama means ‘tale of war’.
 
• Great Mughal Emperor, Jalal Ud-din Muhammad Akbar, commissioned the Mahabharata to be translated into Persian. The translation was carried out by Faizi (brother of Abu’lFazl) and Abd al-Qadir Bada’uni (1540 – 1615).

questions.question: Which planet moves in the opposite direction than other planets in Solar System?
questions.solution:
Uranus is the planet which moves in the opposite direction than other planets in the Solar System.

 
• Not only Uranus but Venus too has a retrograde rotation, i.e. they spin counter to the rotation of the Sun.
 
• The rotation in the same direction as the Sun rotates is termed as prograde rotation.

• Lord Mahavira's name prior to acquiring the Knowledge was Vardhman.

questions.question: Under the Indus Water Treaty, India has not been given the exclusive right over which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
Under the Indus Water Treaty, India has not been given the exclusive right over the river Jhelum.

 
• The Indus Waters Treaty was signed by the then Prime Minister of India Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistan's President Ayub Khan on 19 September 1960.
 
• The treaty deals with the river Indus and its tributaries that flow in both the countries and how it will be utilized.
 
• The deal is classified into two categories, the Eastern Rivers,and the Western rivers. The Eastern Rivers include Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi, while the Western Rivers include Jhelum, Chenab, and Indus.

• As per the Treaty, the Eastern Rivers are to be governed by India, while the Western rivers are to be taken care by Pakistan.
 
• As Indus flows from India, 20% of its water is allowed to be used by the country for power generation, irrigation, and transport purposes.

questions.question: Who was awarded the 2018 Padma Bhushan Award in the field of Art-Music?
questions.solution:
The 2018 Padma Bhushan Award in the field of Art-Music was awarded to Sharda Sinha.

 
• Ms Sharda Sinha is a folk-singer from Bihar.
 
• She is best known for her Chhath Puja themed songs.
 
• Ms Sinha, who is already a Padma Shri recipient, received Padma Bhushan on the eve of Republic day, 2018.
 
• Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award in the Republic of India, is awarded for distinguished service of high order.
 
• It is preceded by the Bharat Ratna and the Padma Vibhushan and followed by the Padma Shri.

questions.question: The Attorney General of India is appointed by whom?
questions.solution:
Attorney General of India is appointed by the President of India.

 
• Attorney General of India is the Indian government’s chief legal advisor and its primary lawyer in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Under Article 76 (1), The President of India shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney General for India.

questions.question: Which plant tissue is also known as growing tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Meristematic tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Meristematic tissue is also known as growing tissue.
 
• Meristematic tissues are responsible for the growth of the plant.
 
• They consist of immature cells which have the power to divide.
 
• On the basis of their position in the plant, meristems are apical, lateral & intercalary.

 
 

 
 
Apical Meristem

 
 
 
Increase length at the tip of the plant

 
 
 

 
 
Lateral Meristem

 
 
 
Increase diameter, the thickness of the plant

 
 
 

 
 
Intercalary Meristem

 
 
 
Increase the length of organs like leaves and internodes

 
 
 

Meristematic tissue__:

 
• Growing regions of the plants are called Meristem.
 
• Meristematic tissue has the capability of cell division.
 
• It is round, oval, and multisided.
 
• It grows and constitutes the different parts of the plant.

**There are three types of meristematic tissues-**

 
• Apical meristem- these are located at the shoot tips and root tips.
 
• Intercalary meristem- located between permanent tissues, at the leaf base and nodes.
 
• Lateral meristem- located at the sides(edges).​

questions.question: Who launched the ‘National Biopharma mission’ named ‘i3’ in June 2017?
questions.solution:
Dr. Harsh Vardhan launched the ‘National Biopharma mission’ named ‘i3’ in June 2017.

 
• Under the National Biopharma Mission, the government launched a programme named **Innovate in India (i3). **It aims to create an enabling ecosystem, in order to promote entrepreneurship and indigenous manufacturing in the sector. 
 
• In the global biopharmaceutical market, currently India has only 2.8% share, the program, however, aims at elevating this to 5% .
 
• i3 is a flagship program of the Government of India in collaboration with World Bank.
 
• Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) will implement the mission.

questions.question: In December 2017, SEBI tightened rating agency norms. The net worth requirement for rating agencies has now been increased from Rs. 5 crore to _________.
questions.solution:
In December 2017, SEBI tightened rating agency norms. The net worth requirement for rating agencieshas now been increased from Rs 5 crore to Rs. 25 crore.

 
• It imposed a 10 per cent cap on cross-shareholding of credit rating agencies, raised their net worth criteria to Rs. 25 crore from the current ₹5 crore and disallowed any seat on the rival’s board.
 
• Moody’s, S&P, and Fitch are the three of world’s largest Credit Rating agency.
 
• Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was established in 1988. It got its statutory mandate and powers under the SEBI Act, 1992.

questions.question: In April 2017, Agriculture Ministry Unveiled Model APMC Act. The new Act proposes to put a Cap on Mandi taxes at what rate (in percent) for food grain?
questions.solution:
Agriculture Ministry Unveiled Model APMC Act. The new Act proposes to put a Cap on Mandi taxes at 8 (in percent) for food grain.

 
• Its aim is to give more freedom to farmers to sell their produce and ensuring that the farmers are not exploited by intermediaries
 
• Farmers are required to sell their produce via auction at the mandi in their region.

questions.question: The ratio of change in velocity of a body to the total time taken by it is its __________.
questions.solution:
The ratio of change in velocity of a body to the total time taken by it is its acceleration.

 
• Acceleration, a = frac{{{{Change in velocity}}}}{{{{Time Taken}}}}
 
• Acceleration of a body is defined as the rate of change of its velocity.
 
• It is a vector quantity and its S.I. Unit is ms⁻².
 
• Velocity of a body is the displacement undergone by the body per unit time.

questions.question: The greater the difference in _________, the faster the air moves.
questions.solution:
The greater the difference in pressure, the faster the air moves.

 
• Air moves from high pressure towards low pressure.
 
• The air in the lower atmosphere is denser than the air lying above.
 
• Therefore, air pressure below is more than above.

questions.question: In Microsoft Word, under paragraph formatting _________ is used to align paragraph on right, left and centre.
questions.solution:
In Microsoft Word, under paragraph formatting Alignment is used to align paragraph on right, left and centre. 

 
• Paragraph formatting refers to formatting features that get applied to an entire paragraph or paragraphs, but not to any given character or a group.
 
• It has following options:
 
 
• Paragraph Alignment
 
• Paragraph Indentation
 
• Paragraph Spacing
 
 
 
• The alignment of a paragraph can be left, center, right, or justify (low, medium, and high).
